A plan covers what its asker thought to ask for. Most people ask for the idea and for what moves. Nobody asks what the site does on a phone, or without the 3D, or what a shared link shows, and a script that leaves those out is half a script. # Storyboard — Marta Kowalczyk

Concept: the RIBA Plan of Work, stages 0–7, grouped into six chapters. Object: eight timber-frame member cross-sections (posts, a beam, a joint), the shape of the cabin's frame going up. Question: **What makes a building worth keeping?**

## The chapters

| Chapter | Its name in the form | The role it holds | What you read | What the pieces do | What you can touch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0–1 · Strategic Definition & Briefing | The opening | Her name, title, the question, one proof | Scattered, flat, unsorted, as if just delivered | Scroll on; nav rail fades in |
| 2 | 2 · Concept Design | Where from | Where the idea comes from — and, in her case, where *she* comes from instead | Still scattered; four pieces lift in turn as origin tags appear | Nothing yet — a reading beat |
| 3 | 3–4 · Spatial Coordination & Technical Design | How | "I'm the project architect from technical design to handover — not the concept" | Members converge and lock at one joint; camera pushes into it | Tap the joint to flip between real details |
| 4 | 5 · Manufacturing & Construction | What | The work built — the cabin, the two sites | Members rise one by one into a standing frame, tied to scroll | Tap a rising member to open its photo |
| 5 | 6 · Handover | What came of it | The real figures, each labelled for what it is | Frame stands at one side; stat cards slide in like a schedule | Tap a card to expand its story |
| 6 | 7 · In Use | The close | The answer; what's still open; the invitation | Frame stands whole, lit, her name on the ridge beam | Contact, CV, LinkedIn |

No "what others say" chapter — there are no quotes in the material. Gap stands; see `decided-for-you.md` and the list below.

## The beats

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | Its caption |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.1 | 1 | Scattered flat across the lower third of the screen, loose, unordered | Plain timber grain, no imagery yet | Her name and title fade in; the question types on; one proof-line beneath it; nav rail fades in | "Marta Kowalczyk — Associate, Field & Rowe Architects, Glasgow. What makes a building worth keeping? Calder Court: 96 flats, retrofit, completed 2025." |
| 2.1 | 1–2, scroll-linked | Still scattered; four pieces lift slightly in sequence as the visitor scrolls, one per origin | Each lifted piece's face carries a plain texture standing for its origin — grain for the workshop, a page-like surface for the book, a simple mark for each school | Four short callouts appear in turn, tied to each piece | "My father's workshop." / "A book of Swiss timber joints, mine since I was nineteen." / "Gdansk Polytechnic Institute, BSc Architecture, 2013–2017." / "Clyde School of Architecture, MArch, 2019–2021." |
| 3.1 | 1 | Members draw together toward one point | Plain timber | Text sets up the claim before the joint locks | "Associate at Field & Rowe since August 2025. On Calder Court and Kirk Street, I'm the project architect from technical design to handover — the detailing, the wall build-up, the site. The concept isn't always mine." |
| 3.2 | 1 | Locked at the joint; camera pushed in close on its face | The joint's face shows one real detail, tappable to the next: the 1:5 wall build-up (if the practice agrees), the school's structural section (hers — she did the structure), or a cabin joint (always hers) | Tap affordance, small label naming the drawing and project | "Calder Court, wall build-up, 1:5." / "A School That Grows, structural section — my part of a team of four." / "The cabin's own frame, drawn by hand, then in CAD." |
| 4.1 | 2–3, scroll-scrubbed | Members rise one at a time from flat to upright, pinned to scroll position | Each riser's face shows a real photograph as it rises — cabin build progression, first post to last shingle; Calder Court site; Kirk Street site (if cleared) | A running, time-lapse-style line of small captions | "Cabin at Kashuby, Poland. 28 m², timber frame. Designed and built with my father, 2021–2022." |
| 4.2 | 1 | Frame fully risen, standing | Wide view against the finished cabin / site photos | Nothing added | "Built, not only drawn." |
| 5.1 | 1–2 | Frame stands to one side; four to five cards slide in front like a schedule sheet | Each card: one figure, qualified | Cards, each its own caption, no umbrella caption needed | "96 flats, Calder Court, retrofit, completed 2025." / "68% less heating demand — modelled, not yet measured. Monitoring starts this winter." / "6 flats, Kirk Street, a church hall, completed 2023." / "Shortlisted, Scottish Timber Schools 2024 — team of four; structure and sections mine." / "28 m², the cabin, 2021–2022." |
| 6.1 | 1 | Frame whole, centred, lit, slowly settling | Her name lettered along the ridge beam | The answer to the question; what's still open; the invitation; contact | *Answer line: hers to write or approve — a draft is offered below, not assumed.* "Calder Court's 68% is modelled; the building is being watched this winter to see if it holds. I still teach Year 2 at Clyde, one day a week. If you have an old house, a small plot, or a class that wants a critic — I'd like to hear from you." |

**Draft answer line, for her to keep, change or cut:** *"A building earns keeping the same way a joint earns trust — not by the idea, but by whether the detail holds."* This is offered as copy, not fact; nothing else in the storyboard states an opinion this directly, and she should read it before it ships.

## Someone with thirty seconds

The first screen carries her name, her role, the question, and one proof-line (Calder Court's headline figures) without scrolling. A nav rail, visible from the first screen on, jumps straight to any chapter by name (Opening, Where from, How, What, Outcomes, Contact). One link in the rail — "Contact" — skips straight to beat 6.1 from anywhere on the page.

## Without the scene

| Where | What the visitor gets |
|---|---|
| On a phone | The same six chapters and all the same text and photographs, in the same order. Fewer members on screen at once (four instead of eight) rendered more simply; the scroll-scrubbed rise in chapter 4 becomes a shorter crossfade between four standing states rather than a continuous drag. Nav rail becomes a bottom sheet opened by one tap. Tap targets enlarged for the joint and the cards. |
| With reduced motion | No continuous or scroll-scrubbed movement anywhere. Each beat appears as its settled state and crossfades to the next on scroll, at a fixed, gentle pace. Same text, same images, same order. |
| With no WebGL | The 3D scene is replaced, beat for beat, with a flat image or simple line drawing standing in for that beat's settled state — e.g. beat 3.2 becomes a photograph of the real detail drawing with the same caption, beat 4.1 becomes the cabin's own time-lapse photographs placed in a column. All text and captions are ordinary HTML and are present regardless. |
| With no JavaScript | A plain long-page document: her name, the question, and the same six chapters' text and photographs top to bottom, in reading order, ending with contact details. No 3D, no animation, nothing missing that the other rows have. |

## The look and the type

The object's material is structural timber — a post, a beam, a joint — so the look should read as workshop and drawing board, not screen-gloss. Three candidates; she picks once there's something to scroll through.

**A — Drawing board.** Ground: warm cream, the tone of tracing paper. Ink: soft near-black graphite. Accent: a single terracotta-red, an architect's pencil colour. Pieces: pale, visible-grain timber with fine linework etched onto their faces, as if drawn on rather than photographed.

**B — Night site.** Ground: charcoal near-black, a site at dusk. Ink: warm off-white. Accent: work-light amber. Pieces: dark-stained timber, grain picked out by the amber light, as if lit by a floodlight on scaffolding.

**C — Lime and linen.** Ground: pale limewash grey, the colour of breathable render — a nod to retrofit. Ink: deep slate-blue. Accent: a muted moss green, echoing Calder Court's winter gardens. Pieces: raw, untreated spruce, pencil-thin annotations.

Two typefaces throughout: a plain humanist sans for all body text and captions; and, for whatever is lettered directly onto the timber's faces (labels, the title block, her name on the ridge beam at the close) a technical, drawn lettering face — the kind used to title a hand-drawn sheet, not a screen UI font.

## Everything else the site needs

| | Build, later or never | Who decided |
|---|---|---|
| The way round the page | Build — the nav rail and the skip-to-contact link, covered above | Decided for her, as part of the thirty-seconds requirement |
| A page for each project | Later — not needed for the one-scroll story; worth it once there's more built work to deep-link to | Decided for her — ask if she wants it sooner |
| Every project listed | Later, paired with the above | Decided for her |
| How to reach her, and a CV | Build — the site's whole purpose is people finding her | **Ask her** — need the actual email or form address, and whether a downloadable CV is wanted at all given the site now tells that story |
| What others say | Never, for now — no quotes exist in the material | Decided for her — a gap, not a decision to drop it forever. Add a chapter if she ever gets a line from the partner, a client, or a student |
| Languages | Undecided | **Ask her** — she trained in Poland, works in Glasgow; unclear if Polish matters to her audience |
| What a shared link shows, and the site's icon | Build — a preview image and title for shared links, and a favicon, both needed if the point is to be found and passed on | Decided for her |
| The page for an address that is not there | Build — small, and should fit the world (a blank sheet, or a snag that can't be found) | Decided for her |
| A blog | Never, for now | **Ask her** — if she wants to write about retrofit or teaching later, this can change |
| A chat | Never | Decided for her — nothing in her goals calls for it |
| A legal notice | Build, if a contact form or any analytics collects data — she is in Scotland, UK GDPR applies | Decided for her as a default; confirmed once the contact method is chosen |
